$meta.name: JRK Analytics Design Tokens
$meta.description: Single source of truth. Run `npm run build` to regenerate dist/. Never hand-edit dist/.
$meta.look: Apple. macOS/iOS grouped surfaces, system greys, systemIndigo accent, Inter as the SF stand-in, compact non-touch density for 1920x1080 desktop.
$meta.$surfaceNote: Apple GROUPED style: the page is tinted (#f2f2f7) and the CARDS are white. That is the inverse of a conventional dashboard, and it means the chart surface is #ffffff in light and #1c1c1e in dark — never the page.
$meta.$appleNote: Values are Apple's system colours verbatim wherever they clear WCAG. Where Apple's own value fails — systemGray as body text is 2.92:1, three of four status marks are under 3:1 on light — the token is darkened and the deviation is noted on the token.
$meta.validated: Categorical palette passes the dataviz six-checks in both modes on both pairlists. Run `npm run validate` after any color change.

ramp.$comment: Apple system greys and the systemIndigo family. Semantic tokens below reference these; components never reference a ramp step directly.

neutral.$comment: systemGray6 -> systemGray, then the dark-mode greys. Light half is Apple's light system greys; 700 and below are Apple's dark system greys.

color.$comment: Semantic color tokens. Every entry has a light and dark value; dark is SELECTED for the dark surface, never computed from light.

surface.$comment: Apple grouped hierarchy. Light: tinted page, white cards, white popovers that lift on shadow + hairline rather than fill. Dark: near-black page, #1c1c1e cards, #2c2c2e popovers — Apple's own dark grouped steps, on a macOS page rather than an iOS one (see canvas).

canvas.$darkNote: NOT #000000. iOS grouped dark uses true black, but on a 1920x1080 desktop it produces halation against near-white text and reads as a void rather than a page — macOS window backgrounds sit near #1e1e1e for exactly this reason. #141416 is ramp neutral-925. It costs elevation: the card is a 1.08:1 fill step off the page here versus 1.23:1 on black, which is why border.subtle.dark is lifted to carry the card edge instead. It also earns the shadow tokens back — a black shadow renders nothing on a black page and reads faintly on this one.

tinted.use: KPI band, highlighted tiles — soft indigo wash

thumb.use: the floating thumb of a segmented control — must be LIGHTER than the track in both modes, which surface-raised is not in dark (it equals surface-subtle)

banner.use: sheet title bar — the one heavy element in a dense report

disabled.$darkNote: Was #1c1c1e, which equals surface.default — so a disabled control on a card had no fill at all, while the light pair (#f2f2f7 on white) reads as a clear tint. #242426 is ramp neutral-875 and restores the same relationship. Disabled fills are exempt from the contrast gate, so nothing caught this.

text.$comment: Apple label colours where they pass. muted is DARKER than Apple's systemGray (#8e8e93) on purpose — systemGray measures 2.92:1 on the canvas and fails AA as body text. Apple accepts that for tertiary labels; we do not.

primary.$darkNote: Apple's dark label is pure white, and that is the one place the value is adopted and then backed off. #ffffff on the #1c1c1e card measures 15.9:1 and on the old black page 21:1 — far past AA, and the excess shows up as glare and halation on 42px semibold hero figures. #ebebf0 is Apple's own dark secondaryLabel base tint at ~92% white: 14.3:1 on the card, 15.5:1 on the page, still triple the 4.5:1 floor.

secondary.use: supporting copy, labels — Apple secondaryLabel base

muted.use: axis ticks, captions, placeholders — darkened from systemGray to clear 4.5:1

disabled.use: disabled label — decorative only, never load-bearing

link.use: inline links, accent text — dark is lightened, systemIndigo is only 3.36:1 on the dark card

border.$comment: Apple separators. Cards on a tinted page separate by fill AND a hairline — Apple grouped lists always draw the rule. In dark the hairline does MORE of that work than in light, because the page-to-card fill step is only 1.08:1; both dark steps are lifted off Apple's systemGray5/4 for that reason.

subtle.$darkNote: Was #2c2c2e, which is 1.22:1 on the #1c1c1e card — a card edge that vanished at desktop viewing distance and left tiles floating. #333336 measures 1.35:1 on the card and 1.46:1 against the page, so it is the load-bearing edge now that the fill step is only 1.08:1.

default.use: card edge, input borders — systemGray4 / opaqueSeparator
default.$darkNote: Lifted from #38383a for the same reason as subtle.

strong.use: axis, baselines, dividers needing weight — opaqueSeparator

accent.$comment: systemIndigo, Apple verbatim. White on #5856d6 measures 5.65:1, so the fill needs no darkening — unlike systemBlue, which does.

onSolid.use: label ON the solid accent — white in BOTH modes; black on the dark indigo is only 4.15:1

wash.use: selected row tint, soft badge fill

status.$comment: Apple system colours for the marks; darkened steps for text, because Apple's own systemGreen/Orange/Yellow fail 4.5:1 as text on white. Reserved meanings — never reused as a chart series, which is why green and red are held out of the categorical palette entirely.

focus.$comment: Apple's focus ring is a soft accent halo rather than a hard outline. base.css draws it as a 3px ring at reduced alpha plus a 1px solid core.

ring.use: focus ring core — must clear 3:1 on page, card, and inset well

offset.use: ring offset, so the ring reads on any surface

chart.$comment: Data-viz layer. Categorical order is the CVD-safety mechanism — assign slots 1..N in order, NEVER cycle. A 9th series folds into 'Other' or facets. Scatter/bubble/choropleth/small-multiples cap at 3 series (all-pairs validated).

categorical.$derivation: Seeded from Apple's system colours, then ordered by search to maximise the WORST ADJACENT pair across BOTH modes jointly — only neighbours touch in a stack or a line chart, and the slot->hue mapping has to be one fact or a series would change hue when the theme is toggled. Apple publishes no CVD-safe categorical sequence (systemRed beside systemGreen is the textbook protan collapse), so the order is derived, not adopted. Blue is pinned to slot 1: it is the default single-series colour used by every bar list, cell bar and sparkline, so it has to be the neutral one — the unconstrained optimum put orange there, which reads as a warning. systemGreen and systemRed are held out entirely (status good/critical — a green or red series in a financial chart reads as a verdict) and systemIndigo is held out as the UI accent. Result: worst adjacent CVD deltaE 16.3 light / 15.1 dark, roughly double the previous palette.

slots.apple: systemYellow, darkened into the lightness band
systemBrown, chroma raised to clear the floor

reliefRequired.note: Sub-3:1 on the white card. Apple's system colours are bright, and a white card is the least forgiving surface for them. Ship visible direct labels or the table view when these are fills. Not dismissable.

tint.$comment: Pastel fills for LARGE marks whose identity is already carried by an axis label, a direct value label, or a number in the legend. Deliberately outside the lightness band and under the chroma floor, so they cannot do identity work and the validator skips them. Using a tint where color IS the identity channel is a bug no gate will catch.
tint.rule: legal only when the mark is axis-labelled, direct-labelled, or accompanied by a value in the legend

ink.use: label set inside a tint fill

ordinalFloor.note: Ordinal ramps must clear 2:1 vs surface. The white card is less forgiving than a tinted one, so the light floor sits deeper than it would on a grey page.

diverging.note: systemRed <-> systemBlue with a NEUTRAL grey midpoint. Equal step count per arm. Never a hue at the midpoint, never a rainbow.

chrome.$comment: surface is the CARD, not the page — that is what chart marks sit on and what the validator measures against.

family.$comment: Inter first, everywhere. SF Pro cannot be shipped — no webfont, and the outlines are Apple's — so the previous SF-first stack meant Apple hardware and Windows rendered in different typefaces, and the tracking below could only be right for one of them. Inter is the closest widely-available SF analogue and it is the one the library is now tuned against. -apple-system and 'Segoe UI' stay as fallbacks so a failed font load degrades to the platform UI face rather than to Arial. Delivery is css/fonts.css.
family.sans: Inter, 'Inter var', -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, sans-serif
family.mono: ui-monospace, 'SF Mono', SFMono-Regular, Menlo, 'JetBrains Mono', Consolas, monospace

feature.$comment: Inter carries SF-ish alternates behind OpenType features; base.css applies this on body so every consumer gets the same shapes. cv05 gives lowercase l a tail, which is the one that earns its keep here — property codes and unit numbers are full of l / I / 1 and Inter's default straight l is ambiguous in all three. ss03 rounds the quotes and commas. Both are silently ignored by a font that lacks them, so the fallbacks in family.sans stay safe. Tabular figures are NOT set here — they are per-context via .jrk-tabular, because a standalone hero figure reads better proportional.

size.$comment: Apple's type ladder adapted for a dense desktop dashboard. md (14px) is body.

tracking.$comment: Negative tracking on display sizes is most of what makes type read as Apple. SF tightens optically as it grows and Inter does too — its opsz axis (14..32, requested in css/fonts.css) is what does it — so these values carry over from the SF-first stack unchanged. Do not add more negative tracking to compensate for Inter; opsz and these tokens already stack.

radius.$comment: Apple corners are TIGHTER than most web design systems — macOS controls sit near 6px and cards near 10-12px. The previous 10/14/18/24 read as friendly-web, not Apple.

shadow.$comment: Apple leans on hairlines and material, not drop shadows. These are deliberately faint. In dark mode the lightened surface and the hairline are still the primary elevation cues, but now that the page is #141416 rather than true black the dark shadows do render — faintly, which is the intent. They rendered nothing at all against black.

size.$comment: macOS-compact, non-touch. These displays are 1920x1080 with a mouse, so the 44px touch target is dead weight — and 1080px of HEIGHT is the real constraint, which is why the vertical rhythm tightened too.
size.$minTouchNote: 24px is the WCAG 2.2 AA floor (2.5.8 Target Size Minimum), down from the 44px AAA touch target. Do not go below 24.

sheet.$comment: Spreadsheet density, tightened further for non-touch. Fixed track widths, because the Excel-style column bar can only line up with the data if every row shares one track list.
sheet.label: 98px

motion.$comment: Apple easing is a gentle ease-out; transitions are quick and small. All wrapped in the prefers-reduced-motion guard in base.css.
